Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the GlobalBank Holdings fourth quarter Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] Please note this event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to review GlobalBank Holdings's results for the fourth quarter. With me this morning are Johnathan Hale, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Thompson, Chief Financial Officer; Michael Patel, Chief Risk Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Credit Officer; and Raj Singh, Chief Technology Officer.

Before we begin, let me remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of these factors.

I will now turn the call over to Johnathan Hale.

Johnathan Hale:
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. GlobalBank Holdings delivered excellent results in the fourth quarter, demonstrating the strength of our franchise and our ability to navigate a dynamic market environment.

Our key priorities for this year remain focused on expanding our market share, improving our efficiency ratio, strengthening our balance sheet, investing in our people, driving innovation, and meeting our ESG goals.

To illustrate our progress, let me highlight our key strategic initiatives and the substantial headway we've made across our three-pillar strategy: accelerating digital transformation, expanding our ecosystem through partnerships, and pursuing sustainable growth in high-potential areas. These have fueled 12% year-over-year revenue growth and expanded our CET1 ratio by 150 basis points to 12.8%, keeping us well above regulatory levels.

On digital transformation and enhancing customer experience, we've committed more than $450 million this year to our Digital First platform, built on AWS cloud-native architecture with generative AI akin to advanced industry pilots. Our mobile app now delivers hyper-personalized product recommendations based on machine learning from anonymized transaction data, lifting cross-sell ratios for deposits and credit by 28%. Digital channels handle 67% of interactions, up from 52% last year, with active mobile users surging 32% to 14.2 million. Our in-house graph neural network for real-time fraud detection has cut false positives by 40%, averting $120 million in losses year-to-date—beating ABA benchmarks.

In North America, we've grabbed 15% digital deposit share among millennials and Gen Z, tracking neobank leaders. Europe benefits from PSD3 via open banking APIs connecting 250 third parties, boosting AUM 22% through embedded finance. In APAC, WeChat Mini Program integration in China has spiked engagement 45%, despite PBOC data rules.

Shifting to ecosystem expansion with fintech partnerships and embedded finance, we're leveraging open platforms rather than solo builds. Our Plaid tie-up enables smooth BNPL via UniPay, handling $8.7 billion in volume this quarter—up 55% year-over-year. Stripe collaboration captures 10% of U.S. Midwest SMB payments, drawing $2.1 billion in new deposits. Our BlackRock Aladdin co-branded wealth product added $15 billion in AUM, with fees up 18% to $220 million amid equity gains and rate cut bets. In India, Razorpay partnership embeds micro-lending in e-commerce, originating 1.2 million $450-average loans at 2.1% delinquencies using RBI-compliant alt-data scores. Ecosystem revenues now form 24% of non-interest income, up from 16%, buffering NIM pressures from the yield curve.

For sustainable growth and ESG efforts, amid Tier 1 climate regs under Basel IV and ECB guidelines, we've pledged $50 billion in green finance by 2025, deploying $28 billion year-to-date—including $12 billion for Texas solar and North Sea wind projects. Our Sustainalytics-benchmarked ESG engine approves 85% of deals, securing $3.4 billion from green bonds at Libor +45 bps. Our Future of Work lending for gig workers, like income-smoothing akin to Affirm but balance-sheet backed, grew 40% to $1.8 billion outstandings at 22% ROE. Latin America shines via Nubank Brazil partnership, scaling remittances and micro-savings to 5 million users with 60% growth amid nearshoring. EMEA challenges from MiFID III are countered by 15% RegTech compliance savings.

Operationally, we've rationalized branches—closing 120 low-performers, opening 35 digital hubs—dropping cost-to-income to 54% from 58%. RPA and GenAI back-office tools yield $180 million run-rate savings, with 12% headcount productivity gains. Zero-trust cyber framework aced Fed tests, plus quantum-resistant encryption ahead of NIST.

These deliver 35% digital revenue share up 900 bps year-over-year, record NPS of 78, and ROTE at 11.2%. Q4 should see $500 million NII lift from 25 bps Fed cuts, backed by $10 billion buyback authorization for 10-12% EPS CAGR to 2026. We're executing amid geopolitics, AI shifts, and consumer changes for top risk-adjusted shareholder returns.

I'll now turn the call over to Sarah Thompson to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, Johnathan, and good morning. GlobalBank Holdings reported net income of $1.8 billion for the fourth quarter, or $1.62 per diluted share. Our results reflect strong revenue growth, disciplined expense management, and a healthy credit environment.

Net interest income increased 9% due to higher loan volumes, deposit growth, and improved margins from our funding mix. Non-interest income rose 12%, driven by fee income expansion and trading gains. Our efficiency ratio improved to 55.1%.

Let me expand on some key drivers starting with our deposit franchise, a bedrock of funding stability and NIM expansion in this higher-for-longer rate world with Fed funds at 5.25-5.50%. Total deposits hit $285 billion, up 12% year-over-year and 4% quarter-over-quarter, beating FDIC peer averages of 7-8%. This is our 10th straight quarter of over 10% annualized organic growth, sans brokered funds. Customer deposits are 92% of funding, down slightly as we cut wholesale reliance to 8%, keeping deposit costs at 2.85%—up just 25 bps sequentially versus 40-50 bps peer spikes.

By mix: Transactional deposits—demand, NOW, money market checking—at $114 billion or 40%, flat sequentially but +2% YoY. Consumer grew 5% via payroll ties to Uber/DoorDash; Southeast (Florida/Georgia) holds 15% SMB share via Business Hub APIs for ACH/wires in QuickBooks/Xero. Amid 45-50% industry betas, we managed outflows from commercial shifters.

Savings—statement, high-yield, premium MMAs—reached $100 billion or 35%, +18% YoY, +6% QoQ, topping 12% national pace. Tiered APYs to 4.75% for $250k+ beat Ally/Marcus by 50-75 bps; 'Boost' app nudges auto-swept $8 billion consumer inflows. Commercial treasury locked $12 billion C&I; West Coast +25% YoY offsets Midwest SVB echoes.

Time deposits—CDs/IRAs—at $71 billion or 25%, doubled YoY, +12% QoQ as clients lock 5.00-5.25% amid inversion signaling cuts. Retail $22 billion, brokered via StoneCastle/Q2; Northeast HNWI arbitrage drove 40%.

Betas at 65% overall (30% transactional, 70% savings, 95% time) aided 15 bps NIM to 3.65%. Non-transactional now 60% mix, trimming HQLA to 18%, LCR 125%. Trends: fintech caps transactional, MMF flows to savings.

Strategies: AI 'Smart Saver' app lifts conversions 20%, Plaid Open Banking pilots. 0.50% relationship bumps retain 92%; no rate wars, NIM guide 3.50-3.75%. $500 million Sun Belt branches, UK Barclays +£2 billion. Stress-tested liquidity $90 billion unencumbered; core beta sub-5%.

Next, our technology investments and their impact on efficiency. In razor-thin margins against Nubank/Chime, we've made tech core, spending $1.4 billion last year—12% of opex, +22% YoY—for 3.2x blended ROI via savings, revenue, risk cuts.

Pillars: Core modernization Phase 2 to Temenos Transact hit 92% STP for retail loans (from 68%), mortgage approvals to 48 hours; commercial reconciliation errors -28%, +15 bps NIM. AI/ML with AWS SageMaker/Google Vertex: fraud engine on 2.5 billion txns at 98.7% accuracy saved $185 million (+35%); chatbots handle 67% Tier 1 queries, -22% calls, CSAT 87%, redeployed 450 FTEs, cost-to-income 54.2% vs. McKinsey 58%.

Cloud: 85% hybrid Azure/AWS, $220 million savings, 1,200 mainframes gone -41% data costs; Apigee APIs 5,000+, $145 million B2B lending fees.

Regional: NA digital 76% txns, +12% cross-sell at -18% costs; Europe PSD2 A2A 14% share, +7 pts efficiency; APAC mobile $0.14/tx -32%, LatAm Ripple blockchain remittances to 8.2 million users, 16.4% ROE.

Aligns composable banking, API economy to $15T/2030 Deloitte; Basel IV/DORA stress-tested, zero incidents. 2024 $1.6 billion, 40% GenAI wealth copilots with BlackRock, quantum encryption; pilots +25-30% advisor productivity vs. HSBC 61% efficiency.

Delivered 17% efficiency to 55.1%, $450 million savings, 9% pre-provision profit; EPS +8-10% 2024.

On capital ratios, CET1 14.2% fully loaded, +40 bps QoQ from 13.8%, +110 bps YoY; transitional 14.7% tops peer median, beats DB/SG amid provisions.

Tier 1 15.8%, +1.6% AT1 from €1.75 billion 5.875% notes.

Reqs: CRR2/CRD5 CET1 min 10.8% (4.5% P1, 1.5% P2R ECB SREP, 2.5% cons, 0.5% CCyB DK), +2.0% G-SIB =11.8%; 245 bps surplus ~€18 billion. Tier 1 13.3%, 250 bps excess. US eSLR 5.6% vs 5%.

Drivers: 60 bps organic from €1.4 billion NI, 12% RoTE, €1.1 billion retained post €0.35/share div 40-50% payout; €500 million buyback of €3 billion auth.

RWA €510 billion flat, credit -1% €380 billion IRB PD/LGD gains post ECB TRIM; market €90 billion FRTB; op €40 billion conduct offset fintech outsources.

YoY +110 bps despite Basel IV 30 bps hit vs peers 50-70 bps.

Regions: Europe 14.5% >11.9%; Italy NPE guarantees; US 13.9% CCAR clear; APAC 16.2% HKMA.

Cap Opt 3.0: €150 million AI RWA, ML 50 million obligors +15 bps/qtr; €5 billion RMBS/CLO SRT €10 billion risk 20 bps; DTA €2 billion green credits.

Allocates €10 billion excess: 40% wealth (Julius Baer UHNW), 30% txn bank €400 billion payments, 20% ESG €50 billion CRR3 green factors. €1.2 billion Q4 buyback, 1.4x div cover.

Guide 14.5-15.0% YE, Basel IV 50 bps buffered 200+ bps; EBA stress 400 bps drawdown >320 bps median.

This fortress supports growth amid volatility.

We are on track for annual targets.

Michael Patel:
Thank you, Sarah. From a risk perspective, we are closely monitoring interest rate volatility and geopolitical tensions. We are taking proactive steps to mitigate these risks through enhanced hedging, scenario planning, and diversified exposures to maintain a strong risk profile.

Lisa Chen:
Good morning. Our credit quality remains strong with non-performing assets at 0.72% and net charge-offs at 0.50%. We are actively managing our loan portfolio and remain confident in our ability to navigate the current economic environment.

Turning to provision for credit losses, we recorded $1.25 billion this quarter, up 12% from Q2's $1.11 billion but flat year-over-year. This included an $850 million ACL build, lifting reserves to $28.5 billion or 2.65% of loans held for investment, +15 bps, with 285% coverage of criticized/classified.

Under CECL since 2020, across $1.07 trillion loans: Consumer 42% drove 45% or $560 million PCL; delinqs +25 bps to 3.45%, cards 4.2%/3.85% NCOs like Cap One. Auto steady 1.8% prime focus. C&I 35% $420 million, 0.45% NCOs, retail/leisure PD +10-15%. CRE 18% $210 million, office $48 billion cap rates 7.5% LGD 35%, but 65% floating. Others $60 million.

Macro 60%: base GDP 1.8% 2025, unemp 4.4%, 10yr 4.2%; 25% downside rec 5% unemp -5-8% houses, ECL 1.12% +20 bps; infl 2.6%, HY spreads +15 bps $15 billion lev loans.

Regions: US 75% Southeast hurricane $75 million; Europe €120 million Stage 2 8%; APAC -10% China stimulus.

Methodology: PD/LGD/EAD segments/FICO/LTV/ratings; vintage ML 25 million accts GenAI NLP sentiment +12% accuracy; Moody's/S&P CCAR/DFAST pass CET1 12.1%; CRE DCF appraisals; overlays $200 million geo/energy, $150 million SMB fraud. 12-qtr forecasts Bayesian; sens +100 bps Fed $400 million PCL.

Ahead peers ACL 2.65% >JPM 2.4%; de-risk CRE paydowns $5 billion, non-accrual 0.85%; asset-based 60% adv rates. Q4 $1.1-1.3 billion no recession.

On reserves, provision $285 million with $210 million net ACL build vs Q3'23 release/$120 million Q2'24; YTD $720 million +15%.

Rationale: macro GDP 1.8% 2025 term rate 4.75-5%, infl 3.5%; 35% stress unemp 5.2%. CRE 22% $140 million, office 8% PD 2.1% vacancy 19%, crit $4.2 billion +12%; consumer 45% $50 million delinq 0.92% subprime auto LGD, cards 3.85% NCO. Charge-offs $75 million 50 bps ann, recov 45%.

Regions: US 65% SE/TX resilient; Europe 12% SME ECB PMI<45 $40 million; APAC release China corp caution.

ACL $8.95 billion 1.54% loans +14 bps >FDIC 1.28%/peers BoA 1.42%; NPA 0.72% cov 214%; Texas ratio 18%.

Since CECL 1.15% to now $2.1 billion builds. Q4 $200-250 million unemp<4.5%; unfunded $1.2 billion 1.1%.

Tech: Black Knight/XGBoost 15 million pts -22% uncertainty; Placer.ai mobility.

De-risk CRE trim $1.5 billion, consumer +8% Prime card, $500 million SRT. CET1 12.8% for growth/M&A.

Prudent build for 12%+ ROE.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator:
[Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from Mike Johnson with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Mike Johnson:
Good morning. Can you elaborate on your technology investments and their impact on efficiency?

Johnathan Hale:
Good morning, Mike. Absolutely, as Sarah detailed, our $1.4 billion tech spend yielded 3.2x ROI, with Temenos STP at 92%, AI fraud savings of $185 million, cloud $220 million cuts, and regional wins like APAC transaction costs down 32%. This drove efficiency to 55.1% and positions us for 8-10% EPS growth in 2024. It's a true moat.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Jane Patel with Wells Fargo. Please go ahead.

Jane Patel:
What is your strategy for deposit growth and mix going forward?

Sarah Thompson:
Thanks, Jane. We've grown deposits 12% YoY to $285 billion with disciplined betas at 65%, transactional steady at 40%, savings exploding 18% on competitive APYs, and time doubling on rate locks. Strategies include AI Smart Saver, relationship pricing, Sun Belt expansion, and Open Banking—aiming sustained funding for loans at sub-5% betas and NIM 3.50-3.75%.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Tom Reilly with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Tom Reilly:
How are you addressing provision for credit losses amid rising delinquencies?

Michael Patel:
Hi Tom. Our $1.25 billion PCL reflects CECL foresight on consumer cards at 3.85% NCOs, CRE office pressures, and macro downside with 2.65% coverage topping peers. Proactive de-risking like CRE paydowns and ML models keeps non-accruals at 0.85%, with Q4 guide $1.1-1.3 billion barring recession.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Grant with Citigroup. Please go ahead.

Lisa Grant:
Can you update us on reserve coverage ratios and build rationale?

Lisa Chen:
Good morning, Lisa. The $210 million net build lifts ACL to 1.54% or 214% NPA coverage, 18% Texas ratio—above FDIC/peers—driven by CRE PD rises, consumer LGD, macro tweaks to 1.8% GDP/5.2% unemp stress. Backed by advanced modeling, we're set for moderation if data improves, supporting 12% ROE.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the conference back over to Johnathan Hale for any closing remarks.

Johnathan Hale:
Thank you for your interest in GlobalBank Holdings. We appreciate you joining us today. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
